posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
two of them are basically memory allocation errors.
that can have a number of different causes:
- your computer does not have enough RAM
or
- you have installed one plugin twice in your plugin list
or
- you have two incompatible plugins clashing with each other.
The second error (of NULL) means that the engine was told to access a data object that does not exist.
that can be
- a missing configuration in one of your plugins
or
- plugins installed in the wrong order (or missing)
or a few similar things.
so to help we need
1) full screenshots of your plugin manager with the list of all plugins and their order
2) your computer specifications, especially RAM and display chip

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
your yanfly plugins are in the wrong order
please check the main list on yanfly.moe for the correct order and change that.
you can add other plugins between them, but yanfly's plugins have to be in exactly the order given or they can cause a lot of strange effects and bugs.
additionally, resorting plugins will make all current savefiles incompatible.
so after resorting you'll have to start a new playtest game, you cannot load older savefiles.
please do so, and if errors happen again then provide new screenshots of them as well as screenshots of the resorted plugin manager.
There are probably several bugs and errors, but we need to search for them one after another and solve each independently.

It usually happens when a teleportation event triggers or when I use an item. Let me explain how these events work: My game is a survival and exploration title based on the urban legend of the “backrooms,” and each level has its own set of maps with the same aesthetic. These levels also have sub-levels that are somewhat similar to a level, as they usually have their own aesthetics, events, and enemies as well. The player has the following needs:
-Health
-Stamina
-Temperature
-Hunger
-Thirst
-Sanity
-Oxygen
To advance to the next level or sub-level, the player must find the exit of each map in the current level up to a certain number:
Every time the player finds an exit, one point is added to the exit counter, and two switches are activated: “Reset Events” and “Subtract Needs.”
When Reset Events is triggered, a common event is activated that deactivates the Temporary Light and Spot Light switches. This controls the lighting system for each level, since in some levels the light usually turns off after a while, and in others there is little or no light.
The Entities switch is also activated, since there are certain items or events on some levels that disable the appearance of enemies in the game; to prevent it from remaining off, this event activates it if there are no other events or items to deactivate it. Then, wait 10 frames before the Reset Events switch turns off:
And the event that reduces needs causes players to lose health, hunger, thirst, and sanity. If the hunger or thirst value reaches 10 or higher, a message appears warning the player that their needs are very low, since once they reach 0, the player loses health every time they find an exit and the teleportation event is triggered. Here is the event:
Once the events are reset and the player's needs are subtracted, +1 is added to the exit counter, and a check is made to see if the exit counter is greater than or equal to the exit parameter (which defaults to 10). If this condition is not met, the player is randomly transported to any of the maps in the level, but if the exit condition is met, the conditional statement is triggered, which randomly determines whether the player finds an exit, remains in the level, or triggers a level event. Whenever one of the exit events is triggered, the exit counter resets to 0. I’ll leave you some screenshots of the teleportation event from one of the levels; it’s very long, so I’ll put it in a spoiler:
Spoiler:
Teleportation Event
At the beginning of each level, the following events typically occur:
-Item spawner: Triggers a common event that spawns a set number of items specified in the event, along with item parameters.
-Item parameters: Sets the maximum number of items and entities that appear across all maps in the level, as well as their spawn probability.
-Object Contents: Sets the objects that can be found in bags and chests within the levels.
-Level Message: A message that informs the player which level they are on; it only triggers when the player advances to a new level. While remaining on the current level, the message stops appearing unless the player goes to another level and returns to the same one. It also determines whether the player will encounter a special entity while sleeping in the level.
-Disable swimming mode: Disables swimming mode if the player advanced to a new level by swimming or diving. The swimming and diving system works with a boat.
-Wi-Fi: The Wi-Fi level of the level; this is usually present on all maps within the level, if the level has Wi-Fi.
-Temperature: Determines the temperature of the level. If the temperature is very high, the player becomes much thirstier when the need loss switch is activated; however, if the temperature is very low, the player loses health if they are not wearing a coat as an accessory. The temperature is usually set only at the start of the level, but in some levels it changes depending on the map, so I’ve included this event on other maps as well.
-Level Visual Effect: Determines the level's lighting; if fog is enabled, the level's lighting will not activate if the temporary light event is present on the map
-Region Teleporter: Activates the teleportation event described above if the player reaches the edge of the map
As you can see, there are a lot of events that trigger when the teleportation event starts and at the beginning of each level. I may have forgotten to mention something, but honestly, I don't know what could be going wrong, since I've checked everything several times and nothing seems to be wrong.

This is far too complex for any general bughunt.
You have to determine the exact point of where and when the crash happens, no other choice.
And that means you'll have to add messages and status indicators to the screen to allow you to tell the exact moment in which part of which event the game is when it crashes.
Without that info finding the bug would be random chance.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
basically any error "of undefined" means that the engine has been given a reference to a data object that does not exist.
if there was a check for isdead then that reference most likely was to an actor, because only actors can be dead in the game.
however one of the most common causes for this type of type error is loading an incompatible savefile, because people rarely go to the database and delete actors already used in their project.
given that the error happens or not based on activating and deactivating a plugin:
are you always starting a new playtest game after changing the plugin configuration?
because changing the plugin configuration is making older savefiles incompatible most of the time, and that effect can easily be done bye loading a savefile from the different configuration.

posts.author: Robro33
posts.body:
When you run that as is, youll crash any time you dont have 4 actors in the party.
change each of your IFs to
Code:
if ($gameParty.members()[x] && $gameParty.members()[x].isDead())
or use a forEach loop on members()

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Additionally to the above, removing an actor from the party will resort the party index.
so if multiple actors are dead, then even four or more actors will not prevent the sequence above from crashing. because if the first and the third actor in the party are dead, then the third check after removing two will go to the former fifth actor.
The second would already be skipped because after removing the first dead actor the second actor now has the index 0 but the second command goes to index 1, which now contains the former third actor.
The entire command structure should be turned into a loop over all party members, checking each index multiple times until one actor is not dead.
